text:
sara: quick sync after the RFC1; we didn't lock runtime semantics for transpose + scaling. need a clear default.

anya: saw small drift in canary when scaling after transpose (post-scale). accumulates in attention logits for longctx.

michael: two choices: pre-scale (apply scale before transpose) or post-scale. pre-scale reduces bias but may force copies when strides mismatch.

kevin: rounding choice affects bias vs determinism. stochastic helps accuracy but breaks reproducibility; nearest-even is cheap and repeatable.

anya: canary numbers: post-scale + nearest-even showed ~0.3% token-prob drift on summarization slice. worth addressing.

sara: proposed runtime defaults: pre-scale + per-tensor nearest-even. offer canary opt-in: pre-scale + per-channel stochastic. also expose header for legacy post-scale requests.

michael: implement a stride-aware pre-scale fastpath to avoid copies for common shapes; buffered transpose only for misaligned dims. i'll prototype.

kevin: document accumulator rules: fp8 paths -> fp16 accumulate; int8 -> int32 accumulate. note this in runtime contract.

anya: test plan: harness that runs combos: pre/post x per-tensor/per-channel x nearest/stochastic over 1k prompts; report tokenwise diffs and KL.

sara: config sketch (informal): quant.profile, quant.transpose_strategy, quant.scaling.granularity, quant.scaling.rounding, and x-kv-precision-boundary-idx header.

kevin: stochastic rounding only in hosted canary by default; must be opt-in.

anya: clients that switch precision mid-sequence must include kv boundary index in header so runtime validates cache alignment.

michael: runtime should return 4xx with diagnostics on mismatch and refuse unsafe cache use.

sara: action items: anya -> implement fastpath + harness; michael -> perf microbench A100/L4; kevin -> docs for accumulator/rounding; sara -> update RFC and canary plan.

deploy-bot: kicked off canary smoke for quant-runtime branch :gear: (logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/11001).

sara: thanks all, will move RFC to implementation_pending if canary stays green.
